title: Play Hide-and-Seek With Airport Sniffer Dogs
summary:
Would you like to play hide-and-seek with a dog at the airport — and help keep people safe? The Transportation Security Administration, or TSA, is looking for volunteers to do just that.

The volunteers act as decoys for the TSA's dogs, which are trained to sniff out explosives. Each volunteer plays a 'covert role player': a pretend passenger carrying a 'training item' around the airport. You might wait in the ticketing lobby, go through security, or sit near a gate. Then the dog team tries to sniff you out.

The TSA says a shift 'may feel like a high-stakes game of hide and seek.' But the game has a serious job: it keeps the dog teams ready for real work. It copies real life, so dogs stay sharp.

A shift takes about two to three hours. You need to be at least 18 to sign up on your own, but younger volunteers can join with an adult, in limited ways. You need to be happy moving around an airport; wheelchair and scooter users can take part too.
why_it_matters: It shows how a fun game of hide-and-seek can help keep everyone safe when they fly.

background_read: The TSA is the group that keeps airports safe by checking passengers and bags before flights.
Its dog teams are trained to smell explosives, and they need regular practice that feels like real airport work so they stay sharp.
Volunteers help by pretending to be passengers carrying training items, so the dogs can practice finding them.
